[E] normalizes Gamma and is not in it. The text's centralizer argument is right (centralizer of S0 in PSL_2(Z) recomputed directly as {1,S0}); the abelianization argument is right; and a third proof: det E = -(A^2-A+1)(A^2+A+1)(A^4-A^2+1)/A^4 is not a Laurent unit times a square, while bare words have det +-A^(2k).

At zeta_8 with D=diag(1,i): D^-1 M D = A_0[[1,0],[-1,1]], D^-1 J D = i[[0,1],[-1,0]], D^-1 E D = i[[0,1],[1,0]]. So E-conjugation is conjugation by [[0,1],[1,0]] in PGL_2(Z), determinant -1, the nontrivial class of Out(PSL_2(Z)). Bare words become scalar x SL_2(Z); WE and EW become scalar x integral det -1 (60 random words, exact).

Normal form confirmed: with D^-1 S_0 D = vL, L=[[a,b],[c,d]], C(zeta_8)=v[[ic,d],[a,-ib]] and det C = -det(L) v^2. For every nonzero entry, det C/C_ij^2 = det(L)(-1)^(i+j)/x^2 (x=c,d,a,b for ij=00,01,10,11). Outer coset: -1/b^2 at lower-right corner 11, and the wrong sign at every nonzero anchor (540 exact evaluations).

The scalar v is finite and nonzero as argued: GWE is in GL_2(O) at Phi_8, so f lies in O, and f(zeta_8) != 0 iff C(zeta_8) != 0. Transport rule S -> bar(P)^-1 S Q verified identically; bar and boundary operations preserve both cosets; M is the exact raw-bracket matrix of one added crossing, so P^T C Q is again an actual two-box tensor.

DVR argument at Phi_8 confirmed: bar preserves the prime; alpha^2 = det h/det k forces alpha to be a unit (in fact alpha = +-A^j); a rank-one S_0 gives an H_0-invariant line, impossible since H_0 contains [[1,0],[-N,1]] and [[1,N],[0,1]] with distinct unique invariant lines; hence S_0 invertible and c_0 != 0. The similitude hypothesis is not used here.

Integrality step confirmed: W^-1 is Laurent, CW^-1 = fG, so f is the off-diagonal entry and lies in R; u = f(v^T G W w) with u a unit of Z[A,A^-1] forces f = +-A^m. Undoing the seed move leaves f unchanged. Tested with unit and non-unit f.

confirmed: Exact identities (sympy): M,J are G-unitary, (AJM)^3=-I, E^2=(delta^2-1)I, E*GE=(delta^2-1)G, EJE^-1=-J, EME^-1=-A^-2 J M^-1 J; at A_0 the D-gauge gives PSL(2,Z) faithfully and [E_0] is an integral det -1 class, so [E] is not in Gamma.

(1) G(A_n) is indefinite iff n>=7 (delta=-2sin(pi/n)); for every n>=7, odd or even, Gamma_n is the Fuchsian triangle group Delta(2,3,n). Re-derived directly: [M_n] is a primitive rotation by 2pi/n, fixed points of J, JM, M form a (pi/2,pi/3,pi/n) triangle (checked to 1e-48 for n=7..60,101,200,1001), then Poincare. Agrees with McMullen Sec.5 (all p>6) and Dlugie Thm 5.4.

Gamma is projectively the reduced Burau image of B_3 at t=A^-4 (intertwiner diag(A^2,1), scalar A); at A_n this is Funar-Kohno's beta_{-q} with q=exp(2 pi i/n). Their Prop 3.5 plus Lemma 3.4 give Delta(2,3,n) for odd n>=7, so the text's citation is accurate. Dlugie's correction only changes the central part of the linear kernel when 3|n; nothing projective is affected.

(2) Comm^+(Gamma_n)=Gamma_n for n>=7 outside {7,8,9,10,11,12,14,16,18,24,30}: Margulis applies; the arithmetic list was recomputed from Takeuchi's criterion (n<=20000); maximality of Delta(2,3,n) for all n>=7 was re-derived by area enumeration. E_n is a holomorphic side-swapping involution acting on H^2 as the reflection in the side through fix(J), fix(JM); <Gamma_n,E_n> is the reflection triangle group.

(3) One-sided to two-sided: alpha_i^2 is a signed monomial so the relations h_i S = alpha_i S k_i specialize at all but finitely many n; S_n^-1 H_n S_n is a lattice inside Gamma_n of covolume [Gamma_n:H_n]covol(Gamma_n), hence finite index in both Gamma_n and S_n^-1 Gamma_n S_n. S_n is in the commensurator. The kernel of specialization is not used.

(4) Jorgensen-Klein as stated in Inoue Thm 1 and Alaqad-Gong-Martin (arXiv:2107.07034): r-generator non-elementary discrete groups in PSL(2,C), marked generators converging; the limit is discrete non-elementary and the generator map from the LIMIT onto the approximants is eventually a homomorphism. No torsion bound needed in PSL(2,C). Hypotheses hold for <J_n,M_n,E_n,S_n>.

(5) The limit: L^+ is a discrete overgroup of the lattice PSL(2,Z), non-cocompact, and non-cocompact Fuchsian groups have area >= pi/3 (signature formula, enumerated; next values pi/2, 3pi/5), so L^+=PSL(2,Z) and L is the extended modular group.

(6) DVR step is sound (O is bar-stable, alpha a unit, rank-one reduction would give an H_0-invariant line), so [S_n] converges to an invertible [S_0]; the fixed-word relation transports to each A_n; projective equality at infinitely many A_n gives the identity over K.

Independent proof of the limit step without Jorgensen-Klein or the area bound: convergence of the triangle tessellations T_n to T_0 plus strict fundamental domains gives directly S_0=W(J_0,M_0,E_0) and S_n=W(J_n,M_n,E_n) for large n. A floating check (n=501..200001, radius 3, exact PGL(2,Z) labels) is consistent.
problems: No mathematical gap found in the specialization and limit argument of (A). The items below are corrections of scope, wording and sourcing.

'Odd n > 30' is sufficient but not necessary. Gamma_n = Delta(2,3,n) for every n>=7 and the commensurator argument works for every n>=7 outside {7,8,9,10,11,12,14,16,18,24,30}. Oddness is only needed to quote Funar-Kohno, whose Props 3.4/3.5 concern the subgroup generated by squares of the braid generators (Delta(k,k,k) for n=2k); the full image for even n is still Delta(2,3,n).

The sentence 'Adjoining the known E_n supplies the entire circle-preserving extended commensurator' lacks its one-line proof (g in Comm orientation-reversing implies g E_n^-1 in Comm^+ = Gamma_n) and is true only in the holomorphic circle stabilizer PGL(2,R)=Isom(H^2). Admitting anti-holomorphic maps, the commensurator is <Gamma_n,E_n> x <iota>, iota the inversion in the circle. Harmless, since S_n is holomorphic.

Limit step wording: 'It has finite area' should be justified by L^+ containing the lattice PSL(2,Z) with finite index; uniqueness of the pi/3 minimizer is not needed (the index computation area(L^+) = (pi/3)/index >= pi/3 suffices).

Sourcing: the original Jorgensen-Klein 1982 paper was not read by the authors nor by me; the statement rests on concordant secondary statements (Inoue Thm 1; Alaqad-Gong-Martin; Marden Thm 4.1.1 seen only as an excerpt). The elementary tessellation argument in REFEREE.md Section 6(d) removes this dependence and should be recorded as the primary proof or as a backup.

Finitely many n must be discarded where S, det S or the multiplier c has a zero or pole at A_n; the text says 'for all sufficiently large n', which covers it, but the multiplier condition c(A_n) real nonzero (needed for S_n to preserve the circle) should be stated.
kleinian.corrected_statement: Let S in GL_2(Q(A)) be a G-similitude with H = Gamma cap [S]Gamma[S]^-1 of finite index in Gamma (projectively). (i) After scaling, S is regular and invertible at A_0 = exp(pi i/4). (ii) For every integer n>=7, any parity, the image Gamma_n at A_n = exp(pi i/4 - pi i/(2n)) is the Fuchsian triangle group Delta(2,3,n) in PU(G_n) (the form is indefinite iff n>=7), and <Gamma_n,E_n> is the reflection triangle group, E_n being a holomorphic side-swapping involution acting on H^2 as the reflection in the side joining the fixed points of J and JM. (iii) For all but finitely many n>=7 outside {7,8,9,10,11,12,14,16,18,24,30}, S_n lies in the commensurator of Gamma_n in the holomorphic circle stabilizer PGL(2,R), which equals <Gamma_n,E_n> (with anti-holomorphic maps admitted it is <Gamma_n,E_n> x <inversion>). (iv) Since [S_n] -> [S_0] in PGL_2(C), there is one word W in J, M, E with [S_n] = [W(J_n,M_n,E_n)] for all large such n (Jorgensen-Klein plus the pi/3 area bound, or directly by convergence of the triangle tessellations), hence [S] = [W(J,M,E)] over Q(A): [S] lies in Gamma^ext = Gamma semidirect <[E]>.

signedsquare.corrected_statement: No change to Theorem B is needed for the sign step. The identity it uses, in the form actually proved: let C be the 2x2 matrix of reduced raw brackets (<O> = 1, common framing) of the four crossingless fillings of two disjoint four-end boxes in one link diagram. Then at A = zeta_8, for every corner (i,j) in 0/1 labels with C_ij != 0, (-1)^(i+j) det C / C_ij^2 = m^2/t^2 >= 0 with integers m, t, and t = +-1 if |C_ij| = 1; this does not depend on the labelling of the fillings. An outer-coset tensor f*G*E*W with ord_{Phi_8}(f) = 0 has C(zeta_8) = v[[ic,d],[a,-ib]] with ad - bc = -1, hence sign -(-1)^(i+j) at every nonzero corner (-1/b^2 at corner 11), a contradiction. A unit rational seed gives ord_{Phi_8}(f) = 0 directly, so moving the seed is unnecessary. Independently, at A = 1 every outer-coset tensor has a zero entry while link-diagram brackets are +-(-2)^(c-1), so no actual two-slot pattern lies in the outer coset even without a unit seed. The unit seed is still needed for the final step, f = +-A^m.
